title: Tuples, Sets & Dictionaries
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Tuples, Sets & Dictionaries in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Tuple
items.text: A tuple is an ordered collection that is generally immutable. It is commonly written with parentheses.

items.heading: Tuple packing
items.text: Several values separated by commas can form a tuple. Parentheses are often optional.

items.heading: Tuple unpacking
items.text: Tuple values can be assigned to multiple variables at once.

items.heading: Set
items.text: A set is an unordered collection of unique elements.

items.heading: Removing duplicates
items.text: Adding duplicate values to a set does not keep separate copies of those values.

items.heading: Set union
items.text: Union combines elements from both sets.

items.heading: Set intersection
items.text: Intersection keeps elements common to both sets.

items.heading: Dictionary
items.text: A dictionary stores key-value pairs and is written with braces.

items.heading: Dictionary access
items.text: A dictionary value is normally accessed using its key.

items.heading: get()
items.text: get(key) performs a dictionary lookup and can return a default value when the key is missing.

items.heading: keys/items/values
items.text: keys() gives keys, items() gives key-value pairs, and values() gives values.
